entry.evidence: So far, no experimental high-pressure study has been performed on REE-arsenates with the monazite structure, neither synthetic nor natural

sequences.source_document: Publisher XML full text (jats_text), checked against the published PDF

steps.action: Name the gap: the high-pressure behaviour of monazite-type REE arsenates has not been studied experimentally, unlike the phosphates.
steps.quote: So far, no experimental high-pressure study has been performed on REE-arsenates with the monazite structure, neither synthetic nor natural

steps.action: Take expectations from phosphate analogues and theory: bulk modulus rises with smaller REE, the REEO9 polyhedron is compressible and the PO4 tetrahedra are rigid.
steps.quote: point out the relevant role played by the compression of the REEO9 polyhedron, whereas the PO4 tetrahedra substantially act as rigid bodies

steps.action: Design an in situ single-crystal synchrotron XRD study of a natural multi-element gasparite-(Ce) in a diamond anvil cell, plus ambient Raman.
steps.quote: by means of in situ single-crystal synchrotron X-ray diffraction with a diamond anvil cell (DAC)

steps.action: Use the sample chemistry the authors measured earlier by EPMA-WDS (Pagliaro et al. 2022).
steps.quote: has been previously determined by electron probe microanalysis in wavelength dispersion mode (EPMA-WDS) based on eight points of analysis

steps.action: Collect unoriented micro-Raman spectra at room conditions in the 30-1200 and 3200-4000 cm-1 ranges.
steps.quote: Unoriented micro-Raman spectroscopy analysis of gasparite-(Ce) has been carried out, at room conditions

steps.action: Set two pressure ramps on separate crystals in the DAC: methanol:ethanol:water to 9.31 GPa and helium to 22.76 GPa, with ruby pressure calibration.
steps.quote: were selected for two separate high-pressure experiments, performed using a 16:3:1 methanol:ethanol:H2O mixture

steps.action: Collect omega-scan diffraction frames at ESRF ID15b at each pressure point, then index them, reduce them and correct them for absorption.
steps.quote: X-ray diffraction patterns were collected with a MAR555 flat-panel detector

steps.action: Refine structure models in P21/n with JANA2006, with occupancies fixed from the chemistry, Ca excluded and isotropic displacement parameters.
steps.quote: All the structure refinements were performed using the package JANA2006

steps.action: Compare the Raman spectrum with earlier arsenate spectra: here OH peaks appear, which support the previously proposed charge-compensation mechanism.
steps.quote: shows the presence of slightly intense peaks, ascribed to OH− groups

steps.action: Describe the unit-cell evolution: anisotropic compression, and a steeper decrease of the beta angle and of the volume above about 15 GPa.
steps.quote: Although still linear, at pressures exceeding ~ 15 GPa, the monoclinic angle decreases more pronouncedly

steps.action: Fit second- and third-order Birch-Murnaghan equations of state to the combined normalized P-V data up to 15.22 GPa, giving K0 = 109.4(3) GPa (BM2).
Check the adequacy of the BM2 fit with an fe-Fe plot (Figure S1) and against the BM3 fit.
steps.quote: suggests that the refined BM2-EoS curve (reported in Fig. 4) properly describes the elastic compressional behavior of gasparite-(Ce)

steps.action: Fit axial BM2 moduli up to 13.70 GPa and compute the finite Eulerian unit-strain tensor from the helium-ramp data (anisotropy 1.77:1.49:1).
steps.quote: magnitude and orientation of the finite Eulerian unit-strain tensor have been calculated based on the data from the helium ramp

steps.action: Compare the change at about 15 GPa with a similar change reported for synthetic CePO4 at about 11.5 GPa.
steps.quote: a similar behavior of the β,V vs. P trends was also described by Huang et al. (33) for the synthetic powder samples of CePO4

steps.action: Exclude a symmetry-changing phase transition as the cause of the compressional change, from the systematic absences.
steps.quote: suggests that no change in symmetry occurs coupled with the change in compressibility

steps.action: Rule out non-hydrostatic stress as an artefact behind the change, because the crystal was compressed in helium.
steps.quote: we can exclude that the observed change in the compressional behavior may be ascribed to non-hydrostatic conditions

steps.action: Compare the bulk modulus with theoretical arsenate moduli (Li et al. 2009) and with experimental CePO4 moduli: it is lower than theory and the compressibility is slightly higher than in CePO4.
steps.quote: the high-pressure compressibility of gasparite-(Ce) is slightly higher

steps.action: Propose two explanations for the difference from CePO4, the complex REE-site composition or As in place of P, without discriminating between them.
steps.quote: [...] be ascribed to the complex composition of the REE-bearing site in gasparite-(Ce) or to the presence of arsenic

steps.action: Note that the bulk modulus lies between REEPO4 and LaVO4, consistent with the AsO4 tetrahedron having an intermediate volume.
steps.quote: the bulk modulus of gasparite-(Ce) is intermediate between those of synthetic REEPO4 and LaVO4

steps.action: From the m.e.w.-ramp structures, compute polyhedral volumes (VESTA), fit the REEO9 bulk modulus (99(3) GPa), and derive AsO4 rigidity above 2.30 GPa, REE-O bond anisotropy and AsO4 tilting.
steps.quote: leads to a refined bulk modulus of KP0,T0 = 99(3) GPa

steps.action: Check that the REE-O3c distance trend is the same in both ramps (independent crystals and media).
steps.quote: it shows a similar and rather significant compressional trend both in the m.e.w. and helium ramps

steps.action: Keep an increase of the REE coordination number from 9 to 10 at about 15 GPa as the likely cause of the compressional change.
steps.quote: experiences an increase in its coordination number from CN = 9 to CN = 10

steps.action: Analyse REE-O-REE lozenge angles: the opening of the unit I angles stretches the chains along [101].
steps.quote: The only mechanism significantly contributing to the anisotropic compression involves the lozenge-like unit I

steps.action: Compare the angular mechanism with the strain-tensor anisotropy and find them in agreement.
steps.quote: provides the rationale for the anisotropic scheme defined by the finite-strain Eulerian tensor reported in Fig. 7a

steps.action: Retain the equation-of-state parameters, the change at about 15 GPa attributed to the CN increase, and the deformation mechanisms (compressible REEO9, near-rigid AsO4).
steps.quote: leading to a bulk modulus of KP0,T0 = 109.4(3) GPa

tree.answer: High-pressure elastic and structural behaviour of a natural monazite-type arsenate; a compressional change at about 15 GPa
No; unit-cell and structure data are observed, while moduli and mechanisms are inferred by equation-of-state fits and structure refinement
Estimate elastic parameters and describe the deformation mechanisms
Only for the ~15 GPa change: phase transition, non-hydrostatic artefact, or coordination-number increase; composition versus As/P for the difference from CePO4
Partly: a phase transition predicts changed systematic absences, and an artefact predicts dependence on the pressure medium
Set in the laboratory: DAC with two pressure media
Yes, within limits: two ramps agree, and BM2 and BM3 fits give consistent K0
Kept: bulk modulus with uncertainty; mechanism as the likely explanation
Not documented; the acknowledgements thank two anonymous reviewers, but no review file was supplied

end.claim: Natural gasparite-(Ce) has a BM2 bulk modulus of 109.4(3) GPa up to 15.22 GPa; its compression is accommodated mainly by the REEO9 polyhedron (K = 99(3) GPa), with near-rigid AsO4 tetrahedra, and no phase transition occurs to about 21 GPa.

decisive_move.sentence: Fitting Birch-Murnaghan equations of state to the single-crystal P-V data of both ramps up to 15.22 GPa produces the bulk modulus on which the paper's headline claim rests.

gates.evidence: No hypothesis directed the data acquisition: the study fills a characterization gap (§1 ¶2–3). The BM2 fit was checked by the fe-Fe plot and against BM3, and the ~15 GPa change was tested against a symmetry change and a non-hydrostatic artefact (§3.2.1 ¶1, ¶3), but the coordination-number explanation is not tested in a way that could fail. The 15.22 GPa fitting cutoff was chosen after seeing the change in the data (§3.2.1 ¶1); nothing was fixed in advance.

imports.item: single-crystal synchrotron X-ray diffraction at ESRF ID15b
Birch-Murnaghan equation of state and finite-strain (fe-Fe) analysis
JANA2006 and CrysAlisPro structure refinement and data reduction
theoretical bulk moduli of LaAsO4 and CeAsO4 (Li et al. 2009)

novelty_claims.quote: So far, no experimental high-pressure study has been performed on REE-arsenates with the monazite structure, neither synthetic nor natural
no experimental data about the elastic properties of the monazite-type arsenates have ever been experimentally obtained

limits: Composition is none_fits: this is a laboratory characterization (estimation) under set conditions, with no rivals posed before the data; rivals appear only ad hoc for the ~15 GPa change. Sub-claims at other statuses: (1) the CN 9 to 10 increase as the cause of the change is best_explanation (the authors write 'likely' and 'suggests'), resting on the REE-O3c distance and partly on helium-ramp structures they describe as scattered and do not fully report. (2) The presence of OH groups is best_explanation from one ambient Raman spectrum ('suggests'). (3) Composition versus As/P as the cause of the higher compressibility relative to CePO4 is left open. The 15.22 GPa cutoff and the 13.70 GPa cutoff for the axial fits were set after inspecting the data (inference). The strain tensor uses the helium ramp only, without a reason given. The m.e.w. ramp provides the structural analysis but reaches only 9.31 GPa, so the structural mechanism above 15 GPa relies on helium-ramp data. The non-hydrostatic exclusion is an argument from the choice of medium, not a direct measurement. Only one natural composition was studied, so the effect of the multi-element A site cannot be separated from that of As. The acknowledgements say reviewers improved the manuscript, but what changed is not recoverable: no review file was supplied.

disagreements.target: Li et al. (2009) theoretical bulk moduli of LaAsO4 and CeAsO4
disagreements.support: The experimental K0 of 109.4 GPa is well below the computed 124.5-125.1 GPa; the authors note that the same theory also overestimates phosphate moduli.
disagreements.quote: [...] of gasparite-(Ce) (KV0 = 109.4 GPa) is lower than the theoretical bulk moduli determined by Li et al. (38)

disagreements.target: Previous Raman studies of monazite-type LREE arsenates (Vereshchagin et al. 2019; Botto and Baran 1982)
disagreements.support: The Cervandone sample shows OH stretching peaks at 3200-4000 cm-1 that were not reported for the earlier arsenates.
disagreements.quote: Conversely to the previously studied monazite-type LREE-bearing arsenates (Vereshchagin et al. 57; Botto and Baran 14)
